text:
Danger is practically all over now from the typhoon which passed Hongkong yesterday — the second of the current season.
Early this morning it was reported to be filling up after moving it back.

label: text
text: At first it was thought that Macao would suffer but the Portuguese Colony has "nothing to report." As a matter of fact, the barometer there was higher than in Hongkong.

label: text
text: The s.s. "Pawnice" has been sulved.

label: text
text: Normal shipping movements were restored this morning. So far no loss in local small craft has been notified.

label: text
text: 6 a.m.—The typhoon is filling up to the North of Pakhoi (on the southern Kwangtung coast). It went inland between Macao and the French port of Kwang-chewan.

label: text
text:
The lowest, at sea-level, on this side of the harbour was 29.18.
The highest wind velocity was 85 miles an hour, at 8.54 a.m. yesterday. In the 1923 disaster, the windgauge registered much over the 100 miles and hour mark. Force 10 (about 70 miles) an hour was returned from Gap Rock.

label: text
text: ... The lowest barometer reading at the Royal Observatory was 29.262 at 9 a.m. yesterday. At Gap Rock, which was a few miles from the typhoon, the lowest was 28.89 at 11 a.m.

label: text
text: 1. These figures are nowhere near the record. The gentlemen who supplied the "China Mail" with readings yesterday admits that he made a mistake, confusing "28" with "29."

label: text
text: As stated in yesterday's "China Mail," the typhoon moved westwards at about 134 miles an hour, covering approximately 900 miles in 66 hours.

label: text
text: There was nothing extraordinary, said Captain Muir, the lowest reading on his barometer being 29,31. All river shipping was tucked away snugly and had no difficulty in weathering the storm.

label: text
text: From Captain Mair, master of the s.s. "Tung On," the "China Mail" learned something about conditions at Macao yesterday.

label: paragraph_title
text: Macro's Experiences.

label: text
text: A few squalls were felt in the inner harbour. The new reclamation and breakwater works in the outer harbour were not damaged.

label: text
text: Passengers who come over added that there was not much of a blow on shore although the predictions were ominous.

label: text
text: The opinion is that the typhoon continued on its gradual curve—see rough sketch on page seven—and missed Macao by about 50 miles.

label: text
text: Just when it was getting dark yesterday, the Dock Co.'s tug "Henry Keswick" successfully re-floated the s.s., "Pawnee" which had been driven ashore at Chung Hue, the island at the north-western corner of the harbour.

label: text
text: There may have been a few small casualties among the fishing fleet and sampans.

label: text
text: Apparently, the Pawnee has not been seriously damaged, in spite of first reports that she struck a rock. She is now at anchor behind Stonecutters, having been towed there by the "Henry Keswick."

label: text
text: No further report has come in regarding the s.s. "Confucius" and the steamboat "Ding On" (formerly the tug "St. Enoch") which ran aground in Kowloon Bay after dragging anchors, as reported in yesterday's issue.

Passengers on board a boat-towed by the steam-launch "Hoi Hong" escaped with no worse than a ducking about 11 a.m. to day, near the Harbour Office.
The launch was towing, this boat and another. A cargo-boat came along and was blown across so that the rigging became interlocked. The boat sank, but passengers were picked up, together with some of their baggage.

label: text
text: The following ships rode out the storm, moored to typhoon buoys in the harbour yesterday: —"Empress of Russia," "Kaying," "Seistan," "Tangistan," "Apoey," "Taiping," "Sui Sang," "Kalgan," "Pheumpenh," "Anhui" (all British), "West Prospect" (American), and "Tjimanoek" (Dutch).

To-morrow's Forecast.
Till noon to-morrow, the Observatory forecasts:—S.E. winds, fresh, moderating; overcast; occasional rain. This is for Hongkong and that part of the coast between Gap Rock and Lamocks, also Formosa Channel.

label: text
text:
For the coast from Hongkong to Hainan, the prediction is:—S. winds, strong, moderating.
By no means a pleasant prospect for the week-end!

label: text
text: Incidentally the report says: Pressure has decreased moderately at Tokyo and slightly at Haiphong. It has increased considerably at Hongkong, moderately at Pratas, and slightly over Formosa. It is nearly stationary elsewhere.

label: text
text: Rainfall for the 24 hours ended 10 a.m. to-day is 1.9 inches. Total for year 65.49 inches against average of 47.95 inches.

The seizure of a quantity of arms led ammunition was mentioned this morning by Detective Sub-Inspection Lane who applied for a confiscation order before Major Wilson at the Central Magistracy.
A number of militants lying at Yaumati Bay came under the attention of police searchers on the night of June 29, and the arms were found in one of the boats, which was deserted by the occupants.
The total haul was 17 pistols, 2 revolvers, and more than 900 rounds

label: paragraph_title
text: HOME MAILS.

label: text
text: A total of 1,000 bags of mail arrived at the Post Office this morning.

label: text
text: The P. and O. steamers "Macedonia" had 361 bags (letters and papers, London, June 24) and 161 bags of parcels from London.

label: text
text: U.S.A., Honolulu, Japan and Shanghai mail by the s.s. "President Wilson" amounted to 274 bags.

label: text
text: The P. and O. steamer "Kashmir" from Shanghai brought 204 bags. Included in this mail were 13 bags from Europe via Siberia.

label: text
text: Mails also arrived from the North by the P. and O. steamer "Ranpura."

label: paragraph_title
text: OUTRAGE SEQUEL.

label: text
text: COMPENSATION FOR VICTIMS' FAMILIES.

label: text
text: HUNG HỒM INCIDENT.

label: text
text: The Government propose compensating the family of the Chinese_workman killed as a result of a bomb being thrown at Hunghom on March 10 of this year in the sum of $2,000 and to make appropriate payment to the eight injured.

label: text
text: This is in accordance with the notification of the Government in June of last year in which assurance was given that such compensation would be made in cases of death or injury arising directly out of the boycott. The outrage is held to be a direct outcome and in the votes to come before the Finance Committee at this afternoon's meeting provision is made for the expenditure of $3,290 on compensation to the nine families.

label: paragraph_title
text: Police Launch Stranding.

label: text
text: The *stranding of the No. 4 Police launch on July 2 involved considerable damage to the vessel. The votes before the Committee to-day include the expenditure of $1,700 on repairs and stores for the launch and $1,100 on salvage costs, including the hire of the "Henry Keswick" and grant of honorari in respect of special services rendered in connection with the salvage.

label: paragraph_title
text: Rescue Tug Vote.

label: text
text: The Government having agreed to the recommendations of a Committee appointed by the Chamber of Commerce to advise on the subject of the rescue tug "Kau Sing" that certain alterations should be made, to-day's votes provide for the expenditure of $2,715 on closing in the upper-bridge, altering the position of the search light, the supply of a double ended whaler, the fitting of storm shutters to the lower wheelhouse, the stuffing of the mattresses with Kapok and the supply of 50 life-belts and 10 lifebuoys.

label: text
text: The cost of the personnel of the officers and crew of the vessel is $3,180 more than anticipated in respect of the period. July 1 to December 31, this being due to the replacing of the proposed Chinese master by a European master and to the additional appointment of a Chinese quartermaster and six Chinese sailors. A vote for this amount is also included in the supplementary estimates.

label: paragraph_title
text: Kowloon-Canton Railway.

label: text
text: The original '1926 estimates in respect of replacing damaged and worn rails to the Kowloon-Canton railway was $300 as it was not expected that the Fanling branch line would be running and it was hoped to continue the policy of strict economy in regard to replacing of rails. The running of the Fanling branch line and the results of an examination revealing the necessity for immediate replacement of certain portions of the track has necessitated an additional vote of $2,850.

label: paragraph_title
text: Volunteer Firing Courses

label: text
text:
The cost of carriage to and from Stonecutters of Volunteer units firing courses on the range there has proved greater than anticipated and an extra vote for $500 is asked for.
For work carried out in England on the motor car used by the Colony's Commissioner to the British Empire Exhibition before exportation for use locally a vote for $852 is before the Committee.
Expenditure on local secret service work has been greater than was anticipated owing to political troubles and an additional sum of $8,000 is asked for the year.

label: text
text: Owing to the outbreak of Rabies additional Coolie Hire for dog catching has raised the monthly expenditure to $720 and $745 in April and May respectively, and at this average the sum of $4,500 now asked for is required to supplement this vote.

label: paragraph_title
text: Port Works:

label: text
text: An additional vote in respect of Port works,(Reclamation of Quarry Bay Marine Lot 4) is due to the foundation's of certain portions of the sea wall protecting the reclamation being more expensive to construct than anticipated; also to less work being done in 1925 owing to labour trouble, the amount requlred in respect of the undertaking being practically a revote of the unexpended balance on 1925. label: text
text: Four bodies of flood vietilns have so far been recovered from the harbour.

label: text
text:
One was that of a child found near the Kowloon Dock. Two bodies were picked up at Hunghom, and the fourth was the boy which was floating near Pottinger Street (Yaumati Terry what) and attracted the attention of crowds after the passing of the typhoon yesterday.
Owing to the decomposed state of the bodies it was impossible to identify them with the reports made to the police by the relatives of people believed to have been drowned during the storm on Monday morning.

text: NO LIGHTS AGAIN

label: text
text: SHIP CAPTAIN ROUND OVER.

label: text
text: ANOTHER PROSECUTION.

label: text
text: Another prosecution of local sea-going vessels for failing to exhibit regulation lights was heard at the Marine Court this morning, when Captain A. W. Hall (master of the "Pheumpenh") was bound over by Lt.-Com. G. F. Hole, R.N. (Marine Magistrate) in a personal security of $5 to come up for judgment when called upon to do so.

label: text
text: The offence occurred at 11:30 p.m. on June 29, when the vessel was lying at No. 7 buoy.

label: text
text: On Captain Hall entering a plea of "not guilty." Lee-Sgt. Goldsmith gave evidence as to boarding the ship; meeting Mr. Goldberg (officer on watch) who subsequently upbraided the native quartermaster, and to the absence of a light on the bow.

label: text
text: Captain Hall admitted that the light was not burning and His Worship recorded a finding of "guilty."

label: paragraph_title
text: Police Court Staff.

label: text
text: In addition to supplementary estimates for 1926, there are before the Finance Committee today certain supplementary estimates for 1925, these including a sum of $2,050 for salary of extra staff and promoted officers at the Magistracy. The staff at the Central Magistracy was reduced when a separate Magistracy was established in Kowloon. Experience, however, showed that too great a reduction had been made and that the appointment of an Indian Interpreter and a Court Usher in addition to the staff provided for in the 1925 Estimates was necessary. Two clerks received promotion to higher classes during the year and received salaries in excess of the amounts provided for them in the Estimates.

label: text
text: $170 is also asked for in connection with Police Expenditure (cost of 1,000 sets of vehicle plates).

label: text
text: On account of the moulders going out on strike, the cost of production of these number plates was increased and the sum asked for is to cover the difference between estimated and actual cost (from $2 to $3).

label: text
text: The total of the supplementary estimates for 1925 asked for and those of 1926 is $5,282 and $149,586 respectively.
